operations.name: Extract
operations.input: A URL, output formats and optional browser rendering.
operations.output: Markdown or HTML with metadata; a job ID in async mode.

operations.name: Batch
operations.input: A list of URLs and extraction options.
operations.output: A job ID and accepted URL count. Retrieve results when complete.

operations.name: Crawl
operations.input: A seed URL, maximum depth and page limit.
operations.output: A job ID. Retrieve extracted pages as the crawl completes.

operations.name: Map
operations.input: A base URL and optional discovery filters.
operations.output: Discovered URLs and their sources, without page content.

operations.name: Search
operations.input: A query, with optional locale, page and search filters.
operations.output: Search results, suggestions and a search job ID.

behavior.title: Synchronous requests and background jobs
behavior.description: Extraction supports sync and async modes. Batch and crawl return a job ID; poll for completion and paginate results. Webhooks can notify your service when a job finishes.

behavior.title: Rendering and usage
behavior.description: Enable render_js when the page requires a browser. Rendering is slower and uses more credits. Keep API keys on your server; usage is charged to your Geonode account.

behavior.title: Errors and retries
behavior.description: Handle authentication, validation and balance errors explicitly. Respect Retry-After on rate limits. A timed-out submission may still have created a job; avoid blindly submitting it again.

integrations.description: Send JSON requests from your backend. Get Markdown, HTML or URLs back directly, or retrieve results from a background job.

sections.title: Make one synchronous request
paragraphs: Provide your API key through GEONODE_SCRAPER_API_KEY in the environment. Send JSON to the extraction endpoint with the X-Api-Key header.
sections.expected: A successful synchronous extraction returns page content under data.markdown and usage under tokens_charged. Read the HTTP status and error body before treating a response as a result.

sections.title: Design for jobs and usage limits
steps: Use asynchronous extraction, batches or crawls for longer work. Save the returned job ID and follow its status to completion, failure or cancellation.
Set explicit page and depth limits on crawls and paginate result sets.
Handle rate limits using Retry-After. Avoid resubmitting a job blindly if the original request timed out after submission.
If you use webhooks, validate signatures and handle duplicate deliveries before updating downstream records.

guide.intro: Connect a compatible AI assistant to Geonode over remote Streamable HTTP. The assistant discovers tools through MCP and calls them on your behalf; you do not need to install a Python SDK for this hosted connection.

sections.title: Check the connection with one page
steps: Add https://scraper.geonode.io/mcp as a remote HTTP MCP server in your client, using the client-specific Geonode guide.
Refresh the client's tools. Without an API key, the server exposes the extract tool.
Ask: “Use Geonode to extract https://example.com as Markdown, then summarize what the page says.”

sections.title: Move from keyless evaluation to your account
paragraphs: Anonymous extraction is synchronous, with documented limits of five requests per minute, one concurrent request and 100 MB per day. JavaScript rendering and country targeting require authentication.

For account-backed access, configure X-Api-Key through your client's secure header or credential setting. Your plan's usage limits then apply. The client-specific guides describe where to configure the header.

sections.title: Hosted service and local adapters
paragraphs: The verified connection is the hosted remote endpoint. A local launcher or supported self-hosted adapter is a separate future delivery; the hosted API and scraping infrastructure are not included in an SDK installation.

guide.intro: gscraper is the Geonode command-line interface. Use it for one-off extraction, shell scripts, batches and crawls without writing an application.

sections.title: Check the installation and extract a page
paragraphs: Set GEONODE_SCRAPER_API_KEY through your environment or the CLI config file. Run the commands below after installation. Avoid putting a real key into command-line flags or committed files.
sections.expected: The help command lists the available commands. A successful extraction prints a readable result; use --json when a script needs the structured response.

sections.title: Use the result in a script
paragraphs: Read ok before consuming result.data.markdown. Failures include an error object with status, code, message and retryable. The CLI also provides exit codes so scripts can detect failure without parsing a human-readable message.

sections.title: Run larger jobs

code.label: TERMINAL · EXAMPLES
code.value:
gscraper map run https://example.com --search pricing
gscraper batch create https://example.com https://example.org --format markdown
gscraper batch wait JOB_ID
gscraper usage concurrency

paragraphs: Replace JOB_ID with the ID returned by the batch command. Use per-command --help to inspect timeout and polling options before putting a command into a scheduled workflow.

sections.title: Resolve configuration problems
paragraphs: Flags override environment variables, which override the config file. Use gscraper config path to locate the TOML file and gscraper config show to inspect settings with keys masked. If the command is missing on Windows, check the Python Scripts directory on PATH or install through pipx.

guide.intro: Add Geonode web extraction to LangChain through native tools. Start with a direct tool call to check your API connection, then pass the same tools to your agent.

sections.title: Make your first tool call
paragraphs: Set GEONODE_SCRAPER_API_KEY in your environment using the key from your Geonode dashboard. This example selects only extraction, URL mapping and search. It calls extraction directly, so no language model or model-provider key is needed for this first check.

code.label: PYTHON · FIRST REQUEST
code.value:
import os

from geonode_scraper_langchain import build_langchain_tools
from geonode_scraper_tools_core import ScraperToolSettings

settings = ScraperToolSettings(
    host="https://scraper.geonode.io",
    api_key=os.environ["GEONODE_SCRAPER_API_KEY"],
    request_timeout=30.0,
)
tools = build_langchain_tools(
    settings=settings,
    operations=["extract", "map_urls", "search"],
)
extract = next(t for t in tools if t.name == "scraper_extract_content")
outcome = extract.invoke({"url": "https://example.com", "formats": ["markdown"]})

if outcome["ok"]:
    print(outcome["result"]["data"]["markdown"])
else:
    print(outcome["error"]["status"], outcome["error"]["message"])

sections.expected: On a successful synchronous request, the script prints the extracted page as Markdown. A failed API request produces an error envelope instead. This is an example to run with your own key; it does not represent a recorded extraction result.

sections.title: Connect the tools to your LangChain agent
paragraphs: Pass tools=tools to LangChain's create_agent alongside your configured chat model. The integration installs langchain-core; an agent application also needs langchain and the package for its chosen model provider.
Give the agent a specific URL and outcome, such as: “Read https://example.com and explain what the page is for, using the extracted content.” Review the tool result before expanding the workflow.

sections.title: Choose the operations your workflow needs

steps: Extract a single page as Markdown or HTML, synchronously or as a background job.

sections.title: Handle failures and long-running jobs
paragraphs: Check ok before reading result. On failure, error contains the HTTP status, code, message and retryable flag. A retryable failure may benefit from another attempt; an invalid key or request needs to be corrected first.

Set request_timeout for each HTTP response. Retries are disabled by default (max_retries=0). Wait tools poll every 3 seconds with a 60-second polling timeout by default; these settings are separate from the HTTP request timeout.

Keep Processing Mode on Sync (Block Until Done), then select Execute step.
Use data.markdown in the next node. tokens_charged reports the extraction cost.
sections.expected: A successful node execution returns the extracted content. Connect that output to the next step in your workflow after checking it with a single URL.

sections.title: Wait for a job or react to its completion
paragraphs: For asynchronous extraction and batches, enable Wait for Completion where offered. For a crawl, start the crawl, then use Get Status with Wait for Completion enabled.

For event-driven workflows, use Scraper API Trigger with Extract Completed or Crawl Completed. Keep Verify Signature on. Activating the workflow registers its webhook URL; deactivating it removes that registration.

sections.title: Installation and retry limits
paragraphs: This is a self-hosted community node, not an n8n-verified Cloud integration. Update it through Settings → Community Nodes.
The node retries HTTP 429 and 5xx responses with increasing pauses, up to five total attempts, and respects Retry-After. Other errors stop the node and display the API message.

verification.note: Private app access is required. Module/action definitions and output schemas reviewed in source on 2026-10-21; deployed account access and live workflow execution were not tested. No public marketplace listing is verified.

confirmed: Extract page content as Markdown or HTML, with optional JavaScript rendering.

A Geonode API key and an active plan for authenticated requests.

troubleshooting.question: My API key is not accepted.
troubleshooting.answer: Check the key in the Geonode dashboard and send it using X-Api-Key. Keep it out of browser bundles, URLs and version control.

troubleshooting.question: The request is rate limited.
troubleshooting.answer: Respect the Retry-After response and your plan’s concurrency limits. Avoid automatically retrying a job submission when its outcome is unknown.

guide.intro: Use Geonode’s private Make.com app to turn website URLs into content for your scenario. Its source defines 15 modules for extraction, batches, crawls, URL discovery and usage. Request access before searching for it in Make.

sections.title: Set up your first Make scenario
steps: Request private app access from Geonode for your Make organization and zone, then accept the supplied invitation. There is no public marketplace install link yet.
Create a Geonode API key in the dashboard. Add the invited app to a scenario and choose Extract a URL (Sync).
Create an API Key connection. It tests the key against authenticated usage statistics.
Enter https://example.com as URL and explicitly select Markdown in Output Formats; the module defaults to HTML.
Choose Run once. Inspect Extracted Data → Markdown (data.markdown), Metadata → URL (metadata.url) and tokens_charged.
Map the content and source URL into your destination module. Test the complete scenario before enabling its schedule.
sections.expected: A completed extraction returns page content. An accepted connection or a queued job alone does not confirm that the page was retrieved.

sections.title: Example: website content to Google Sheets
paragraphs: Pass a URL into Extract a URL (Sync), then add Google Sheets → Add a Row. Map metadata.url to a Source URL column, data.markdown to Content, and tokens_charged to Usage. The Sheets module requires its own connection.

For summaries, add a separate AI module that reads the Markdown. Product fields, comparisons and change alerts require your own parsing or comparison steps. This is a workflow recipe, not a live-tested blueprint.

sections.title: Choose the right module
paragraphs: Extract a URL (Sync) returns content inline. Extract a URL (Async), Get an Extraction Job and List Extraction Jobs support background extraction. Extract a URL (Wait for Completion) combines submission and polling.

Crawl modules: Start a Crawl, Get Crawl Status, Cancel a Crawl and Start a Crawl (Wait for Completion). Batch modules: Start a Batch Extraction, Get Batch Status, Cancel a Batch and Start a Batch (Wait for Completion).
Map URLs from a Site emits one bundle per discovered link. Get Usage Statistics reads the connected account’s usage.

sections.title: Handle dynamic pages and longer jobs
paragraphs: Where exposed, Render JavaScript and browser wait settings let the page settle before capture. Setting a wait option enables rendering. Proxy country and type are configurable where offered.

Keep the job ID and use separate start/status steps with bounded polling for longer work. Wait helpers hold an operation open; choose their interval and attempt limit deliberately. Do not resubmit an existing job because polling timed out.

sections.title: Make modules or MCP?
paragraphs: This connector provides native Make scenario modules. Web search and webhook triggers are not defined in this Make source. Use the separate hosted MCP server when connecting a compatible AI assistant.
Module definitions were reviewed in source; deployed account access and a complete live Make scenario have not been verified in this review.

guide.intro: Connect web content to a Zap with Geonode’s private app: four actions, a job lookup and a completion trigger. Request a private invitation before configuring your first Zap.

sections.title: Extract your first page in Zapier
steps: Request and accept the private app invitation in the Zapier account you will use.
Create a Geonode API key, then connect the app with that key and base URL https://scraper.geonode.io.
Choose Extract URL, enter https://example.com, use synchronous processing and select Markdown output.
Test the action and map Markdown (data__markdown) and URL (metadata__url) into your next step.
Test the complete Zap before enabling it. The connection test checks authentication; returned page content checks the extraction.

sections.title: Choose an action or trigger
paragraphs: Extract URL retrieves a page. Batch Scrape URLs processes a list. Crawl Site follows links within depth and page limits. Map URLs discovers links under a site.

Find Job by ID retrieves background status/results. Job Completed is a REST-hook trigger for extraction, batch or crawl completion. Keep the submitted job ID and wait for a terminal result before consuming content.

sections.title: Example: a new record to a summary
paragraphs: Use a form or spreadsheet trigger that provides a website URL, extract Markdown, then pass it to a separate AI step. Save the summary with its source URL in your destination app. Each downstream app requires its own connection.
Structured product fields and change detection need separate parsing and comparison steps. These are workflow ideas, not preconfigured or live-tested Zaps.

sections.title: Availability and connection choices
paragraphs: There is no verified public marketplace installation link. Source definitions have been reviewed, but deployed account access and live Zap execution were not tested.
This app provides native Zapier actions. For a compatible AI assistant use Geonode’s separate MCP server; web search is not an action in this Zapier source.
